title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཤ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 106)
shelf_note: Canonical Derge Tengyur Madhyamaka commentary volume (vol. 106 / ཤ), correctly catalogued.

ocr_errors.problem: syllable གང་ (what/which) misread as ན་ in canonical verse quotation
phrase མེད་དེ (has no) misread as མ་ཡིན་ཏེ (is not)

tr_errors_A.problem: first line of the Dharmasaṃgīti sūtra verse quotation ('When feeling is described as experience') omitted

tr_errors_B.english: Wishing to address an opponent's argument that the two truths are untenable, he says if.
tr_errors_B.problem: dialectical speaker reversal: attributes the opponent's opening objection to the author answering an opponent

tr_errors_B.english: By what can the self experience anything?
tr_errors_B.problem: doctrinal distortion: misreads གང་ཉིད་/ན་ཉིད་ to invent 'the self' into a verse demonstrating the absence of any substantial experiencer

tr_errors_B.english: it does not exist as any kind of material thing
tr_errors_B.problem: philosophical term dngos po (bhāva / real entity / substantial existent) mistranslated narrowly as 'material thing'

pages.prefer_reason: Translation A correctly preserves technical Madhyamaka terminology and dialectical debate structure, whereas Translation B reverses the speaker introducing the objection and distorts the Dharmasaṃgīti verse to invent 'the self'.

book_verdict: Clean, authentic woodblock page from the Derge Tengyur Madhyamaka section with high-quality transcription and strong translation in Version A.
